brief_text: a 1 kg ball dropped onto one end of a seesaw throws a 100 g ball resting on the other end at least 50 cm above where it started

usage.text:
The seesaw starts tilted, with the ball's end down against its hinge stop. A small lip holds the 100 g ball in place. The 1 kg weight falls about 1.4 m onto the raised end, about 0.4 m from the pivot, and drives the plank to its opposite stop. That flings the ball upward.

My hand estimate for the ball's launch speed is about 4 m/s, which would carry it roughly 0.8 m up, comfortably over 50 cm. This is a calculation only; I have not run the scene.

```xml
<mujoco model="seesaw_catapult">
  <option timestep="0.002" gravity="0 0 -9.81"/>
  <worldbody>
    <light name="sun" pos="0 0 3" dir="0 0 -1"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="3 3 0.1" rgba="0.8 0.8 0.8 1"/>
    <body name="base" pos="0 0 0">
      <geom name="base_post" type="box" size="0.03 0.08 0.1" pos="0 0 0.1" contype="0" conaffinity="0" rgba="0.4 0.3 0.2 1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="seesaw" pos="0 0 0.25">
      <joint name="seesaw_hinge" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0" limited="true" range="-0.3 0.3" damping="0"/>
      <geom name="seesaw_plank" type="box" size="0.5 0.06 0.01" mass="0.2" rgba="0.6 0.4 0.2 1"/>
      <geom name="seesaw_lip" type="box" size="0.01 0.06 0.03" pos="-0.49 0 0.04" mass="0.01" rgba="0.5 0.3 0.1 1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="weight" pos="0.38 0 1.8">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="weight" type="sphere" size="0.05" mass="1.0" rgba="0.2 0.2 0.2 1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="ball" pos="-0.4417 0 0.156">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="ball" type="sphere" size="0.03" mass="0.1" rgba="0.9 0.2 0.2 1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
  <keyframe>
    <key name="start" qpos="-0.3  0.38 0 1.8 1 0 0 0  -0.4417 0 0.156 1 0 0 0"/>
  </keyframe>
</mujoco>
```

```expect
weight touches seesaw
seesaw reaches its upper stop
ball rises at least 0.5 m above its start
```

-- STARTS OUTSIDE ITS OWN RANGE ---------------------- joint seesaw_hinge

I was expecting a starting angle between -0.3° and 0.3°, but I found:

    starts at -17.19°, range -0.3° to 0.3° as MuJoCo applies it

MuJoCo would push it back inside its limit in the first few steps: whatever it was meant to do from there, it would not. MuJoCo reads joint ranges in degrees unless <compiler angle="radian"/> is set, but keyframe angles always in radians.

Hint: widen the range or change where it starts

usage.text:
Two fixes, because the joint range was being read in degrees:

- **Range in degrees:** the hinge range is now written as -17.19° to 17.19°, which matches ±0.3 rad. MuJoCo reads joint ranges in degrees by default.

verdict.what_happens: The 1 kg weight falls ~1.4 m onto the raised end of the seesaw at 0.53 s, driving the plank to its upper stop at 0.58 s; the 100 g ball is launched from the lowered end and peaks at z = 1.11 m (about 0.95 m above its 0.16 m start) at 0.96 s before landing and rolling away.

usage.text:
The 1 kg weight falls from 1.8 m and lands on the raised end of the seesaw at 0.53 s. That snaps the plank to its upper stop at about 778°/s by 0.58 s. The 100 g ball leaves the plank at 0.59–0.60 s. It peaks at 1.11 m at 0.96 s, about 0.95 m above its starting height of 0.16 m, and lands at 1.43 s. Afterwards the weight and ball roll off along the floor and the seesaw falls back to its lower stop.
